diagnosis.narrative: The series is dominated by a moderate downward trend (a net fall of ~43% of its level). Seasonality is strong (period 48): a repeating cycle explains much of the movement. The series is quite predictable: its energy concentrates in a few structured frequencies. The series reads as ambiguous by the ADF/KPSS tests. Across validation windows the model ranking is moderate (Kendall tau 0.399), which favours a weighted combination.

action_args.justification: The series is seasonal-dominated (seasonal_strength 0.77) with moderate ranking instability (Kendall tau 0.40) and only 3 validation windows, making weight estimation high-variance. The trimmed_mean over the 7 most stable models (pool2) robustly discards the worst 20% of predictions, which is well-suited to a series where a few models (ARIMA/ETS/THETA group) carry correlated error and one model (DWT_rf) dominates on seasonality. The 'separated' verdict confirms no other strategy in the history is statistically competitive, and the near-uniform inverse-error weights I tested would reduce to a plain mean that already scored worse (a6, -0.0785).

The trimmed_mean over the 7 most stable models (pool2) robustly discards the worst 20% of predictions, which is well-suited to a series where a few models (ARIMA/ETS/THETA group) carry correlated error and one model (DWT_rf) dominates on seasonality. The 'separated' verdict confirms no other strategy in the history is statistically competitive, and the near-uniform inverse-error weights I tested would reduce to a plain mean that already scored worse (a6, -0.0785).
